title: They knew His face… but rejected His voice.
paragraphs: They knew His face… but rejected His voice.
Nazareth wasn’t confused about who Jesus was.
They just couldn’t accept who He claimed to be.
And that tension? It still lives in us.
Because it’s possible to grow up around Jesus… and still resist Him when He gets too real.
They heard Him read Isaiah—“The Spirit of the Lord is upon Me… to proclaim good news to the poor” (Luke 4:18)—and for a moment, they marveled.
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable.
We don’t always reject Jesus loudly.
Sometimes we reject Him quietly… when He confronts the parts of us we’ve learned to hide.
The delayed obedience we renamed “waiting on God.”
The secret sin we buried under Sunday worship.
What version of Jesus are you holding onto?
or the One who confronts you?
Because the real Jesus does both.
And Nazareth wanted comfort without confrontation.

He said no prophet is accepted in his hometown (Luke 4:24), and then He brought up Elijah and Elisha—how God moved not among the familiar insiders, but among outsiders who actually believed (Luke 4:25–27).
They pushed Him to the edge of a cliff.
The same voices that said “wow” were now shouting “kill Him.”
Familiarity with Jesus can become the greatest barrier to surrendering to Him.
and still resist the Savior who calls you to change.
If Jesus never confronts you, you may not be following Him—you may be controlling Him.
A Jesus who never disagrees with your lifestyle.
Some people don’t reject Jesus because they don’t understand Him…
They reject Him because they understand Him too well—and refuse to change.
Even as they tried to kill Him…
Jesus walked right through the crowd and went on His way (Luke 4:30).
Because rejection does not cancel calling.
And here’s where grace explodes into the story.
The same Jesus rejected in Nazareth…
would later be rejected on a cross.
Isaiah 53:3 says He was “despised and rejected by men.”
So that those who rejected God…
They all shouted, “We don’t want Him.”
But Jesus still chose the cross.
Romans 5:8 says while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
While we were still resisting Him.
But grace is not permission to stay the same.
You don’t lose your life in surrender.
The one who sees everything… and still offers you mercy.
The one who will confront your sin… and then carry your shame.
The one who was rejected… so you could be accepted.
Don’t reduce Him to something comfortable.
Receive Him as He is—Lord and Savior.
And maybe this is your moment.
If this pierced something in you, don’t ignore it.
It might expose the one thing you’ve been avoiding.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
